mistakes.text: They filmed the kitchen while they built the rainbow plate.

mistakes.feedback_sk: „Filmed the kitchen“ znamená, že natáčali sami. „Dali natočiť“ je „had the kitchen filmed“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Filmed the kitchen“ znamená, že natáčeli sami. „Dali natočit“ je „had the kitchen filmed“.
mistakes.feedback_en: “Filmed the kitchen” means they did it themselves; use “had the kitchen filmed”.

mistakes.text: They had filmed the kitchen while they built the rainbow plate.
mistakes.normalized: they had filmed the kitchen while they built the rainbow plate
mistakes.feedback_sk: Toto je Past Perfect. Causative má poradie „had + vec + past participle“: „had the kitchen filmed“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Tohle je Past Perfect. Causative má pořadí „had + věc + past participle“: „had the kitchen filmed“.
mistakes.feedback_en: That is the Past Perfect. The causative order is “had + object + past participle”: “had the kitchen filmed”.

mistakes.text: They had the kitchen filmed until they built the rainbow plate.

mistakes.feedback_sk: „Kým“ tu znamená počas toho, teda „while“. „Until“ znamená až dovtedy, kým.
mistakes.feedback_en: Here the meaning is “during that time”, so use “while”; “until” means up to that moment.
